title: A weighted Fourier-coefficient bound for a unit-twisted lift
statement:
Let $k \ge 2$, and let $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ be normalized (that is, $f(0) = 0$) and $\varepsilon$-far from linear for some $0 \le \varepsilon \le 1$, meaning that $\mathrm{dist}(f,g) \ge \varepsilon$ for every linear function $g : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$. Then for every unit $j \in (\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z})^\times$, the $j$-twisted lift $\widetilde{f}_j(x) = \omega_k^{\,j\,f(x)}$ satisfies
\[
  \sum_{s \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n}
    \bigl|\widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s)\bigr|^2 \,
    \operatorname{Re}\widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s)
  \;\le\; 1 - \bigl(1 - \cos(2\pi/k)\bigr)\varepsilon,
\]
where $\widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s)$ denotes the Fourier coefficient of $\widetilde{f}_j$ at frequency $s$.
replaced:

\mathbb{Z}_k^\times$, then
\[
  \sum_{s\in\mathbb{Z}_k^n}
  \bigl\|\widehat{(\widetilde{f}_j)}(s)\bigr\|^2\,
  \operatorname{Re}\!\left[\widehat{(\widetilde{f}_j)}(s)\right]
  \;\le\; 1 - \bigl(1-\cos(2\pi/k)\bigr)\varepsilon.
\]
